items.title: Punch List
items.stakes: 412 open items, nineteen working days, and a list that says sixty things are closed that nobody has seen.
items.reward: A building that opens with its safety, its access and its show — and a list and drawings you can believe.

objectives.text: Decide what you tell the owner
Decide what happens to the sixty
Decide who fixes the drawings, and when

items.rumor: A list is a promise. So is a drawing.

items.alt: The site trailer; the punch list printed on a long roll across the table; Nkechi points at it; Maya faces her.

bubbles.text: Four hundred and twelve. Nineteen working days.

items.caption: Opening night in nineteen working days.

lines.text: Four hundred and twelve. Nineteen days. You do the maths or I will.
Two hundred and eighty-five. Then we choose the other hundred and twenty-seven — with Odile.

items.prompt: 08:15. Odile is coming at ten for an update. What do you tell her?
items.risk: An opening night that discovers what didn't get done.
timeout: She asks Bram to decide. He picks by trade, not by risk.

hints.text: What does the owner need to decide — and what do they need to see?

options.label: “It'll all be done.”
options.result: Nkechi: “At fifteen a day? It won't.”
options.consequence: A promise the arithmetic says no to.

options.label: The arithmetic and a plan: 285 of 412 can close; here they are by risk — life safety, access, the show, operations — and here's what could wait and until when. Her decision, with Bram
options.result: Odile reads it twice, then defers the broadcast room and the cosmetics — in writing.

options.label: Put every crew on overtime for three weeks
options.result: Twenty a day is 380. Still 32 short — with tired crews.

options.label: Close the easy ones first so the number looks better
options.result: The count drops by sixty. The risk doesn't move.

items.title: Sixty closed, none seen.
items.body: Nkechi's closure log has sixty rows marked ‘closed by: trade’ with nothing in the ‘verified’ column — twelve of them signed on the same Friday afternoon. She samples ten. Three aren't fixed: a loop amplifier still in its box, a mislabelled outlet, a cover plate hiding an unterminated cable. Thirty percent. If that holds, about eighteen of the sixty are still open.
items.label: Test: the share — and how many are really still open?

options.result: The loop amplifier is still in its box on opening night.

items.title: The drawing in two halves
items.body: Cologne Cathedral was begun in 1248 and stood unfinished for centuries, a crane frozen on its south tower. In 1814 half of a medieval drawing of its west front turned up in Darmstadt; the other half was found in Paris two years later. Work resumed in 1842, and the cathedral was finished in 1880 — to a drawing more than five hundred years old. A drawing that records what was meant can outlive everyone who meant it.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #80 · AVERY'S LENS  Say the arithmetic out loud  When the work can't all be done in time, show the numbers early and let the owner choose what waits — before the deadline chooses for you.  Fifteen a day for nineteen days is 285. The list was 412. The only question was who would choose the 127 — and when.

items.title: Three revisions behind.
items.body: Kit opens the as-builts to plan the life-safety re-tests. Rack drawing RK-SL2 is at rev C; the building is at rev F. Logic inputs one to eight are drawn, none labelled — nothing says input 3 is a life-safety interface. That's the drawing the tech had when he did punch 188. And it's the drawing the venue's own technicians will run the building from.
items.label: Test: how far behind — and why it matters now?

unknown: What else changed since rev C

options.result: She draws what she thinks is there — and the contract says the contractor delivers them.
options.consequence: The wrong author, and a guess.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the three weeks yourself.

items.alt: The main hall with seats going in; Nkechi, Odile and Maya on the Friday walk, clipboards in hand.

bubbles.text: Seventy-one closed this week. I've seen every one.
And the rack drawings say ‘life safety’ where it matters.

items.prompt: Honestly? I'd rather just grind through the list. Choosing feels like giving up.

options.label: “Choosing is how we make sure the hundred and twenty-seven that wait are the ones that can. Not choosing lets the deadline pick.”
options.reply: …So the list gets an order, not just a length.

options.label: “We'll get through it.”
options.reply: At fifteen a day we won't.

options.label: “Odile will decide anyway.”
options.reply: She can only decide if we show her.

items.body: The closure log: sixty rows with ‘closed by: trade’ and an empty ‘verified’ column. Twelve were closed on the same Friday afternoon by the same sign-off.

And the building's still weeks from finished.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Do the arithmetic on day one (rate = count ÷ time) and show the gap. Order by risk: life safety and access, the show, then what operations needs; the owner decides what waits. “Closed” means the commissioning agent has seen it — sample it (% = part ÷ whole × 100). As-builts are part of the building; fund them and check them against the racks.
REFLECTION (optional)  · What list in your work says “done” for things nobody has seen done?
